digest.headline: Wall Street slumped as tech stocks hit multi-year lows during a regulatory probe.

lede.b: The Nasdaq 100 index had its worst week since 2020. The S&P 500 fell 3.7% in a single day, which is a big drop in the total value of the stock market. Both the S&P 500 and the Dow entered correction territory, meaning they dropped 10% or more from recent highs. Nvidia shares plunged 14% because of a regulatory probe by the government. This tech drop dragged down the wider market and pushed the VIX fear index, which measures worry among investors, to its highest level since April 2025.
lede.i: The Nasdaq 100 recorded its worst week since 2020 as the S&P 500 fell 3.7% in a single day. Both indices entered correction territory alongside the Dow after seven consecutive losing sessions. Nvidia shares plunged 14% during a regulatory probe, dragging down the wider technology sector. Twenty-five S&P 500 stocks hit new 52-week lows and the VIX fear index climbed to its highest level since April 2025.
lede.a: The Nasdaq 100 printed its worst weekly performance since 2020 following a 3.7% single-day drop in the S&P 500. Correction territory beckoned for both the S&P 500 and the Dow after a seventh straight losing session turned the Nasdaq composite negative for the year. Nvidia shares plunged 14% amid an ongoing regulatory probe, triggering sector-wide liquidation that pushed twenty-five S&P 500 constituents to new 52-week lows. Market volatility spiked as the VIX fear index printed its highest reading since April 2025.

items.b: The S&P 500 fell 3.7% in a single day and entered correction territory.
items.i: The S&P 500 fell 3.7% in a single day, entering correction territory after seven consecutive losing sessions.
items.a: The S&P 500 dropped 3.7% in a single session to enter correction territory following seven consecutive losing days.

items.i: The FTSE 100 index declined as a rout in metals and technology stocks outweighed positive retail figures.
items.a: London equities declined as a metals and technology rout overwhelmed positive domestic retail figures.

items.b: The DAX index dropped 7.29% for the week to finish at 24,802.78 points.
items.i: The DAX index dropped 7.29% for the week to finish at 24,802.78 points following a steep producer price jump.
items.a: The DAX index dropped 7.29% over the week to finish at 24,802.78 points amid a steep producer price jump.

items.b: Leapmotor sold 310,052 vehicles and global gold prices fell below $3,550.
items.i: Leapmotor sold a record 310,052 vehicles while spot gold fell below $3,550 after losing the $3,600 level.
items.a: Leapmotor recorded record sales of 310,052 vehicles while spot gold fell below $3,550 after dropping nearly 9% in a week.

thread.b: Global markets faced heavy selling pressure this week. Stock indices in the United States and Germany dropped significantly. Gold prices and the Australian dollar also fell.
thread.i: Equity markets faced synchronized downward pressure as technology stocks and metal prices sold off globally. Major indices in the United States and Germany recorded sharp weekly losses. Currency markets also reflected this risk aversion.
thread.a: Global equity indices absorbed heavy selling pressure driven by technology sector corrections and commodity routs. Transatlantic markets posted steep losses alongside broader currency depreciation against safe-haven flows. Asset prices reacted to localized regulatory actions and shifting monetary policy expectations.

United States of America.label: United States
United States of America.sub: Wall Street slumps as tech stocks hit multi-year lows

stories.t: Nasdaq and S&P 500 Suffer Heavy Losses
stories.b: The Nasdaq 100 index tracks one hundred of the biggest tech companies. It just suffered its worst week since the year 2020. The broader S&P 500 index dropped by 3.7% in a single day. This marked its seventh straight session of losses. Both the S&P 500 and the Dow indices entered a correction phase.
stories.i: The Nasdaq 100 index recorded its worst week since 2020. The S&P 500 fell 3.7% in a single day, marking its seventh consecutive losing session. Both the S&P 500 and the Dow entered correction territory. The Nasdaq composite turned negative for the year.
stories.a: The Nasdaq 100 printed its worst weekly drawdown since 2020, while the S&P 500 dropped 3.7% to cap a seventh consecutive losing session. The broader S&P 500 and Dow indices crossed into correction territory, and the Nasdaq composite wiped out its year-to-date gains. Selling pressure intensified as macroeconomic growth assumptions decoupled from equity valuations.

stories.t: Nvidia Shares Plunge During Regulatory Probe
stories.b: Nvidia is a massive maker of computer chips used for artificial intelligence. Its stock price plunged by 14% over the week. This drop followed news of a regulatory probe into the company. Twenty-five different companies inside the S&P 500 index hit new 52-week lows.
stories.i: Nvidia shares plunged 14% amid a regulatory probe. The drop dragged down the wider tech sector and contributed to twenty-five S&P 500 stocks hitting new 52-week lows. The VIX fear index subsequently climbed to its highest level since April 2025.
stories.a: Nvidia shares tumbled 14% following the disclosure of a regulatory probe. This concentrated tech sell-off forced twenty-five S&P 500 constituents to print new 52-week lows. Concurrently, the VIX volatility index surged to its highest reading since April 2025 as risk aversion dominated.

politics.b: No political events or government policy changes were reported in the market updates for the United States on this date.
politics.i: No political developments or legislative changes were mentioned across the financial market reports for the United States.
politics.a: No sovereign policy shifts or political announcements were recorded in the session data for the United States.

timeline: April 2025
The VIX fear index previously reached levels last seen before climbing to new highs on 20 November 2026.
20 November 2026
The S&P 500 fell 3.7% and the Nasdaq dropped 5.13%, pushing major indices into a correction.

United Kingdom.label: United Kingdom
United Kingdom.sub: FTSE 100 falls on metal and tech rout despite retail data

stories.t: London equities drop despite positive retail figures
stories.b: The FTSE 100 index fell today. An index is a group of stocks tracked together to measure market health. Positive retail numbers came out in the UK. This retail data failed to rescue the index. A rout in metals and tech dragged London lower.
stories.i: The FTSE 100 index declined today. Positive retail data failed to rescue London equities. A rout in metals and technology stocks drove the downward pressure.
stories.a: The FTSE 100 dropped despite positive domestic retail data. A sharp sector-specific rout in metals and technology overwhelmed the consumer figures. London equities closed lower on this broad sectoral divergence.

stories.t: UK inflation acts as invisible tax on cash holdings
stories.b: UK inflation acts like an invisible stealth tax. Inflation means the speed at which prices rise over time. This force reduces the real value of cash savings. Publications highlighted various ways to shield money from this erosion.
stories.i: UK inflation functions as an invisible stealth tax on savings. Rising consumer prices erode the purchasing power of cash holdings. Financial reports outlined methods to shield personal funds from this ongoing depreciation.
stories.a: UK inflation operates as an unlegislated stealth tax on nominal cash holdings. Real purchasing power degrades continuously as the general price level rises. Various protective strategies emerged to help investors shield uninvested capital from this erosion.

politics.b: No political updates were reported for the United Kingdom today.
politics.i: No political updates were reported for the United Kingdom today.
politics.a: No political updates were reported for the United Kingdom today.

timeline: Positive UK retail data released alongside falling FTSE 100 index figures.

Germany.label: Germany
Germany.sub: German stocks plunge and Bundesbank signals rate hike

stories.t: German Stocks Plunge Amid Broad Sell-Off
stories.b: The German DAX stock index tracks the forty biggest companies in Germany. This index fell by 7.29% over the week. Shares dropped as artificial intelligence companies sold off and producer prices jumped. The DAX closed down at 24,802.78 points.
stories.i: The DAX index dropped 7.29% for the week. Equities tumbled as global inflation pressures collided with an artificial intelligence sector correction. The index finished at 24,802.78 points following a steep producer price jump.
stories.a: German equities suffered their worst weekly contraction in over a year as the artificial intelligence trade unwound. The DAX plummeted 7.29% to close at 24,802.78 points. Surging producer prices compound margin pressures for cyclical components within the index.

stories.t: Bundesbank Backs December Rate Increase
stories.b: Joachim Nagel backs a rate hike by the European Central Bank in December. The central bank sets borrowing costs for countries using the euro. He wants policy to turn slightly restrictive. Consumer prices run at an annual rate of 4%.
stories.i: Bundesbank President Joachim Nagel supports a December European Central Bank rate hike. He argues monetary policy should turn slightly restrictive to combat price pressures. Annual price growth currently runs at 4%.
stories.a: Bundesbank chief Joachim Nagel advocated for a December European Central Bank tightening measure. He maintained that monetary policy must shift into restrictive territory. Headline price growth persists at 4%, anchoring the argument for further policy action.

politics.b: German officials manage economic policies as price pressures continue.
politics.i: German monetary authorities address persistent price growth through central bank channels.
politics.a: German monetary policymakers navigate persistent price pressures via central bank alignment.

timeline: European stocks post heavy losses and the DAX drops 7.29% for the week.
Bundesbank's Nagel backs a December ECB rate hike.

Japan.label: Japan

stories.t: MBK Partners Targets Wacom in 1 Trillion Won Buyout
stories.b: MBK Partners agreed to buy Wacom. Wacom is a Japanese maker of digital pens. The price is 1 trillion won.
stories.i: MBK Partners reached an agreement to acquire Wacom. The transaction values the Japanese digital pen maker at 1 trillion won.
stories.a: MBK Partners secured an acquisition agreement for Wacom. The deal values the Japanese digital input device manufacturer at 1 trillion won.

stories.t: Honda and Toyota Recall 1.6 Million Vehicles Over Airbag Risks
stories.b: Honda and Toyota recalled 1.6 million vehicles. The recall involves Takata airbag rupture risks.
stories.i: Honda and Toyota issued a recall for 1.6 million vehicles. The action addresses rupture risks linked to Takata airbags.
stories.a: Honda and Toyota initiated a recall affecting 1.6 million vehicles. The manufacturers cited rupture hazards associated with Takata airbag inflators.

politics.b: Japan's Tashima challenged FIFA boss Infantino. He called for a governance debate.
politics.i: Japan's Tashima challenged FIFA president Infantino. He demanded a formal debate on governance.
politics.a: Japan's Tashima challenged FIFA chief Infantino. He pushed for an institutional governance debate.

China.label: China
China.sub: Corporate milestones, tax measures and market updates

stories.t: Leapmotor records vehicle sales as WeRide hits robotaxi revenue milestone
stories.b: Leapmotor sold 310,052 cars in a record period. A car company makes about €18 on each vehicle it sells. WeRide reached 100 million yuan in global robotaxi revenue for the first time in the third quarter.
stories.i: Leapmotor sold a record 310,052 vehicles while retaining a margin of about €18 per unit. WeRide surpassed 100 million yuan in global robotaxi revenue for the first time during the third quarter.
stories.a: Leapmotor achieved a record volume of 310,052 units with nominal unit economics of approximately €18 per car. WeRide crossed the 100 million yuan threshold in global robotaxi revenue for the first time in the third quarter.

stories.t: Gold prices decline as domestic jewelry rates drop
stories.b: The global gold price fell below $3,550. Spot gold dropped nearly 9% in a week and lost the $3,600 mark. Chinese brands cut pure gold jewelry prices by more than 20 yuan, marking the tenth straight day of declines.
stories.i: Global gold prices fell below $3,550 as spot gold dropped nearly 9% in a week to lose the $3,600 level. Chinese brands cut per-gram prices of pure gold jewelry by more than 20 yuan, extending a downward trend into the tenth consecutive day.
stories.a: Global spot gold fell below $3,550 after dropping nearly 9% over the week and losing the $3,600 handle. Domestic Chinese brands reduced per-gram prices of pure gold jewelry by over 20 yuan, continuing a ten-day decline that exceeds 650 yuan for the year.

stories.t: Huarui Century penalized for net profit inflation
stories.b: China's Huarui Century inflated its net profit by 12.88 million yuan. The company faces an 8 million yuan fine. It will be renamed ST Huarui starting next Tuesday.
stories.i: China's Huarui Century inflated its net profit by 12.88 million yuan. The entity faces an 8 million yuan fine and will change its name to ST Huarui beginning next Tuesday.
stories.a: Huarui Century misstated its financials by inflating net profit by 12.88 million yuan. Regulators imposed an 8 million yuan fine on the company ahead of its renaming to ST Huarui effective next Tuesday.

politics.b: A state newspaper published an opinion piece about the economy. People's Daily stated that those who bet against the Chinese economy will ultimately be proven wrong.
politics.i: People's Daily published commentary arguing that individuals who bet against the Chinese economy will ultimately be proven wrong.
politics.a: People's Daily published an editorial asserting that market participants who bet against the Chinese economy will ultimately be proven wrong.

India.label: India
India.sub: Indian markets hit nine-month highs as foreign buying surges

stories.t: Stock Indices Reach Nine-Month Highs Driven by Bank Shares
stories.src: ANI News · BigGo Finance · HDFC Sky
stories.b: The Sensex and Nifty indices track groups of major company shares, like a basket representing the wider stock market. Both indices reached nine-month highs at the end of the week. Bank shares led this market rally, which means their prices rose sharply. This upward movement pushed the Sensex up by 2,327 points. The winning streak for these indices now extends to four weeks.
stories.i: The Sensex and Nifty 50 finished the week at nine-month highs, propelled by a strong rally in banking equities. Record foreign institutional investor buying lifted the Sensex by 2,327 points over the period. The Nifty 50 touched 25,800, extending a four-week winning streak with weekly gains of 3%. Foreign inflows surpassed 1 trillion rupees.
stories.a: Indian equities decoupled from global sell-offs as the Nifty 50 approached record territory, underpinned by over 1 trillion rupees in foreign institutional inflows. The Sensex advanced 2,327 points to close at a nine-month high, driven primarily by outperformance in banking stocks. Market participation broadened as the Nifty 50 hit 25,800, securing a fourth consecutive weekly gain of 3% despite a broader global market downturn.

stories.t: Shriram Finance Enters BSE Sensex as Torrent Power Plans Bond Offering
stories.b: Shriram Finance will replace Trent in the BSE Sensex index starting on December 21. Meanwhile, Torrent Power announced plans to sell up to 20 billion rupees in bonds, which are fixed-income loans issued to raise capital. Bandhan introduced a new Nifty Commodities Index Fund for investors. These corporate updates coincide with a broader period of heightened market activity.
stories.i: Shriram Finance is scheduled to replace Trent in the BSE Sensex effective December 21. Torrent Power announced preparations for a bond issue valued at up to 20 billion rupees. Bandhan simultaneously launched the Nifty Commodities Index Fund to expand its product offerings. These structural index and corporate debt developments accompany the broader equity market rally.
stories.a: Index provider adjustments place Shriram Finance into the BSE Sensex as a replacement for Trent, effective December 21. Torrent Power initiated marketing for a debt issuance targeted at up to 20 billion rupees. Bandhan expanded its fund suite by introducing the Nifty Commodities Index Fund. These corporate actions proceed alongside record foreign portfolio inflows into domestic equities.

stories.t: Indian Rupee Records Strongest Weekly Advance of the Year
stories.b: The Indian rupee achieved its best weekly gain of the year. The currency climbed to a level of 92.67 against the dollar. Foreign money inflows supported this currency appreciation. The rising exchange rate coincided with record buying in the national stock market.
stories.i: The Indian rupee registered its most significant weekly advance of the year. Sustained foreign inflows drove the currency higher to 92.67. This appreciation mirrors the broader equity market strength driven by foreign institutional investors. Currency gains solidified alongside the four-week stock rally.
stories.a: The Indian currency printed its largest weekly appreciation of the year, strengthening to 92.67. Heavy foreign institutional inflows served as the primary transmission mechanism for the currency gains. This outperformance occurred concurrently with domestic equity indices scaling nine-month highs.

politics.b: No government policy discussions or political updates appeared in this week's financial reports from Indian markets.
politics.i: Government policy announcements and political developments were absent from this week's market reporting.
politics.a: Fiscal and regulatory policy updates remained absent from the primary financial data releases for the week.

Brazil.label: Brazil
Brazil.sub: Petrobras expansion projects and currency-driven commodity drops

stories.t: Petrobras Expands Capacity and Offshore Exploration
stories.src: The Globe and Mail · CPG Click Oil and Gas · EnergyNow
stories.b: Petrobras aims for a capacity expansion of 280,000 barrels per day. The state-backed energy firm also made a fresh oil discovery off the coast of Amapa. Meanwhile, Seagems owners contemplate selling their firm despite securing a $410m contract with Petrobras. Petrobras targets 2028 to finish seismic data collection in the Pelotas Basin.
stories.i: Petrobras pursues a 280,000-barrel-per-day capacity expansion alongside a new oil discovery off the coast of Amapa. Seagems owners consider a sale of the company despite locking in a $410m contract with Petrobras. Petrobras schedules the completion of seismic data in the Pelotas Basin for 2028.
stories.a: Petrobras targets a 280,000-barrel-per-day capacity expansion and announces a new offshore oil discovery near Amapa. Seagems owners explore asset sales despite securing a $410m Petrobras contract for six pipe-laying support vessels. Petrobras sets a 2028 horizon for seismic data completion in the Pelotas Basin.

stories.t: Brazilian Currency Drop Influences Sugar Prices
stories.src: CMB News · CPG Click Oil and Gas
stories.b: The Brazilian real slid in value. This currency slide triggered a sharp correction in global sugar prices. ANP proposed new rules for natural gas auctions under pressure from Petrobras. These new rules pave the way for Braskem to join the Gas Release program.
stories.i: The Brazilian real dropped in value and triggered a sharp correction in global sugar prices. ANP proposed new rules for natural gas auctions following pressure from Petrobras. These proposed regulations pave the way for Braskem to join the Gas Release program.
stories.a: A slide in the Brazilian real sparked a sharp downward correction across global sugar prices. ANP formulated new natural gas auction rules under pressure from Petrobras. The framework paves the way for Braskem to enter the Gas Release program.

politics.b: ANP faced pressure from Petrobras regarding natural gas auctions. Petrobras operates as a state-controlled energy enterprise in Brazil. ANP proposed regulatory updates for the sector.
politics.i: ANP faced pressure from Petrobras to alter natural gas auction rules. The state-controlled producer influenced the proposed regulatory framework. ANP advanced changes designed to incorporate Braskem into the Gas Release initiative.
politics.a: ANP advanced new rules for natural gas auctions under direct pressure from Petrobras. The state producer leveraged its market position to reshape the regulatory perimeter. The revisions create a pathway for Braskem to participate in the Gas Release scheme.

Saudi Arabia.label: Saudi Arabia
Saudi Arabia.sub: Attacks hit Saudi infrastructure and Aramco investments continue

stories.t: Houthi Attacks Strike Saudi Oil Infrastructure
stories.b: Houthi strikes caused extensive damage to the headquarters of Saudi Aramco, which is the state-backed oil giant of Saudi Arabia. State news reports show that these attacks also cut Saudi oil output and flow along the East-West pipeline. The Houthis stated that they targeted Saudi East-West oil transport and vowed to launch more attacks on airports and oil facilities.
stories.i: Houthi strikes inflicted extensive damage on the headquarters of Saudi Aramco, prompting concerns over security at key energy assets. State news confirmed that the assaults successfully cut national oil output and disrupted flow along the East-West pipeline. The militant group publicly claimed responsibility for targeting the transport corridor and vowed subsequent strikes against domestic airports and oil facilities.
stories.a: Houthi assaults delivered extensive structural damage to Saudi Aramco headquarters, serving a direct blow to the kingdom's core economic infrastructure. State news agencies verified subsequent supply disruptions affecting domestic crude output and the throughput of the East-West pipeline. The militant group confirmed the targeting of critical transport vectors, vowing an ongoing campaign against regional airports and hydrocarbon assets.

stories.t: Aramco Ventures Invests in ROTOBOOST
stories.b: Aramco Ventures has put money into a Finnish firm named ROTOBOOST. This investment focuses on methane splitting to help build a hydrogen and advanced materials economy. The deal was announced alongside broader corporate updates from Aramco.
stories.i: Aramco Ventures secured a stake in Finland-based ROTOBOOST to back its proprietary methane splitting technology. The strategic injection explores new production gateways into the hydrogen and advanced materials sector. This transaction coincides with separate marketing events hosted by the broader energy enterprise.
stories.a: Aramco Ventures completed an equity investment in Finland's ROTOBOOST to scale methane splitting applications. The initiative targets technological development within the emerging hydrogen and advanced materials value chain. This venture capital deployment runs parallel to ongoing international branding initiatives by the firm.

politics.b: Government officials managed the aftermath of attacks on vital oil sites and pipelines. Security forces responded to threats aimed at the kingdom's main economic nerve centres. Authorities also pursued international investments to diversify the national economy.
politics.i: State leadership coordinated responses to militant strikes targeting critical hydrocarbon infrastructure and administrative headquarters. Authorities assessed the structural impact on the East-West pipeline and domestic crude output. Policymakers simultaneously maintained outward capital deployments via state-backed venture funds.
politics.a: The administration managed severe operational disruptions following targeted kinetic strikes on core economic nodes. State apparatuses dealt with immediate bottlenecks along export vectors while managing national security repercussions. Strategic capital allocations via sovereign vehicles persisted despite localized infrastructure vulnerabilities.

timeline: Aramco headquarters and the East-West pipeline suffer attacks by Houthi forces.
Aramco Ventures completes an investment in Finland's ROTOBOOST.

Nigeria.label: Nigeria

stories.t: Naira Drops to Five-Month Low
stories.b: The official exchange rate for the Nigerian naira fell to N1,389 per US dollar. This is the weakest level for the currency in five months. Central bank interventions failed to stop a 2.50% drop that touched N1,400. The parallel market traded the currency at between N1,435 and N1,470 per US dollar on November 21, 2026.
stories.i: The official exchange rate for the naira depreciated to N1,389 per US dollar, marking a five-month low. The currency touched N1,400 after a 2.50% fall despite interventions by the central bank. Parallel market rates traded between N1,435 and N1,470 per US dollar on November 21, 2026.
stories.a: Spot rates for the naira printed at N1,389 per US dollar in the official market, establishing a five-month trough. Intraday weakness persisted to N1,400 despite central bank intervention, representing a 2.50% drop. Parallel market quotes ranged from N1,435 to N1,470 per US dollar on November 21, 2026.

stories.t: Foreign Reserves Contract Amid Exchange Rate Pressures
stories.src: Daily Post Nigeria · Daily Report Nigeria
stories.b: Nigeria's foreign reserves dropped to $54.65bn. The reserves lost a total of $406m during this period. Lower foreign currency buffers coincided with the weakening of the naira against the US dollar.
stories.i: Foreign reserves for Nigeria decreased to $54.65bn after shedding $406m. The reduction in reserve assets coincided with the depreciation of the naira.
stories.a: Gross foreign reserves printed at $54.65bn following a $406m draw down. The depletion of external buffers preceded the deeper depreciation of the spot exchange rate.

politics.b: Anambra State leader Soludo provided a 50,000 naira December bonus to civil workers. Katsina governor started a 1.4 billion naira upgrade project for the Ingawa hospital.
politics.i: Anambra State granted civil servants a December bonus of 50,000 naira. Katsina State initiated a 1.4 billion naira renovation project for Ingawa hospital.
politics.a: Anambra State issued a 50,000 naira December bonus to civil servants. Katsina State flagged off a 1.4 billion naira capital expenditure project for the Ingawa hospital upgrade.

timeline: Foreign reserves drop to $54.65bn as the naira hits N1,389 per dollar in official markets.

Australia.label: Australia
Australia.sub: Australian dollar hits lows and equities move on reports

stories.t: Australian Dollar Drops to Ten-Month Lows
stories.b: The currency of Australia, known as the Australian dollar, fell to a 10-month low. This drop happened because expectations for interest rates in the United States and Australia diverged. Interest rates are the cost of borrowing money set by central banks.
stories.i: The Australian dollar declined to a 10-month low, breaking its multi-month range. Divergent outlooks between the Federal Reserve and the Reserve Bank of Australia drove the currency downward.
stories.a: The AUD/USD rate breached its multi-month range to print a 10-month low. Market participants priced in divergent monetary policy paths between the Federal Reserve and the Reserve Bank of Australia.

stories.t: WiseTech Shares Fall Following Recent Decline
stories.b: Shares are units of ownership in a company. WiseTech Global shares experienced a 34% slide. Analysts suggested the stock could trade at a discount despite the drop.
stories.i: WiseTech Global shares absorbed a 34% slide, prompting assessments that the equity could trade at a discount. Analysts reviewed the valuation of the company following the sharp drop.
stories.a: WiseTech Global equities suffered a 34% drawdown, leading to evaluations that the shares might trade at a discount. Market observers recalculated the valuation multiples following the steep correction.

politics.b: Politicians made threats that could impact the economy of Australia.
politics.i: Threats from political figures emerged regarding potential impacts on the Australian economy.
politics.a: Political announcements introduced external risks with potential transmission channels into the Australian economy.
